# Can periodic reward composition teach a biped several common gaits?

> **Current answer:** APEX uses phase-dependent foot-force and foot-velocity rewards to learn and demonstrate walking, running, hopping, skipping, and galloping on Cassie. This does not establish arbitrary humanoids, difficult terrain, or seamless gait switching; transfer requires renewed validation of phase, contact, torque, and fall protection.

## Credibility and review status

- **Handbook level:** `L3 Reviewed engineering conclusion`
- **Level note:** This conclusion has passed the Handbook EngineeringClaim review gate.
- **Confidence:** `0.80`
- **Confidence rationale:** The paper and official code support periodic force/velocity reward composition and Cassie multi-gait demonstrations. Large-scale hardware success rates, cross-robot evidence, and difficult-terrain evidence are absent.
- **Safety level:** `caution`

## Key terms

- Simulation-to-Real (仿真到现实, Sim2Real)
- Proportional-Derivative Control (比例-微分控制, PD Control)
- Actuator (执行器)
- Joint Torque (关节力矩)
- Center of Mass (质心, CoM)

## Applicable robots

- Cassie.

## Applicable simulators

- MuJoCo.

## Controllers and methods

- Recurrent policy with joint PD control.

## Applicable environments

- Periodic flat-ground gaits and simulation-to-real transfer.

## Assumptions

- The phase variable, foot-contact estimate, and low-level PD controller are stable and available.
- Reward phases, actuator limits, and contact boundaries are revalidated on the target platform.

## Result

- APEX uses phase-dependent foot-force and foot-velocity rewards to learn and demonstrate walking, running, hopping, skipping, and galloping on Cassie. This does not establish arbitrary humanoids, difficult terrain, or seamless gait switching; transfer requires renewed validation of phase, contact, torque, and fall protection.

## Evidence

- [Sim-to-Real Learning of All Common Bipedal Gaits via Periodic Reward Composition](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.01387>) — `support/primary`; Figures 2–4, Tables I–II, and Sections III–V.; Defines periodic reward composition and the policy, then reports simulated and hardware results for common Cassie gaits.
